justice: The narrow roadway is almost entirely allocated to motor vehicle use, with nearly no dedicated space reserved for pedestrians and non-motorized traffic.
There is a complete lack of universal accessibility facilities such as tactile paving and curb ramps, creating major barriers for elderly, disabled and wheelchair users.
No equitable spatial provisions exist for vulnerable road users, resulting in highly imbalanced right-of-way distribution across different traveller groups.
safety: Vehicles are parked along both sides of the narrow road, severely blocking sightlines and drastically increasing collision risks for all road users.
No lane markings, crosswalks, speed limit signs or traffic calming facilities are present on this open mixed-traffic road.
Unseparated mixing of large trucks, passenger cars and potential pedestrians creates an extremely dangerous travel environment with no user protection measures.
livability: There are no public resting facilities, street amenities or community leisure spaces along the route, offering almost no support for outdoor resident activities.
The surrounding undeveloped greenery, scattered litter and bare soil result in an unrefined, low-comfort living environment.
Lack of active street frontages results in low natural social surveillance, reducing perceived personal safety after daytime hours.
sustainability: Simple roadside vegetation provides limited ecological benefits and heat mitigation effects for the surrounding area.
No infrastructure to encourage green travel modes like walking and cycling is constructed, further reinforcing car-dependent travel patterns.
The fully impervious road surface lacks sponge city and rainwater management functions, with no sustainable stormwater handling design.
aesthetics: Rows of roadside trees provide basic natural greenery along both sides of the street.
Exposed bare dirt, scattered roadside waste and unmanaged vegetation create an unkempt and visually disordered street appearance.
Large billboards, overhead power lines and unorganized roadside parking significantly degrade the overall visual coherence of the streetscape.
comfort: Sparse tree coverage offers very limited sun shading, resulting in strong sun exposure and poor thermal comfort during daytime travel.
Narrow road width and close proximity to large moving and parked vehicles generate noise stress and significant psychological discomfort for pedestrians.
No resting spots or buffer zones are available along the route, creating notable physical strain for elderly and fatigued pedestrians.
walkability: There is no paved, dedicated sidewalk; pedestrians are forced to walk on uneven dirt shoulders or directly on the vehicle travel lane.
Absence of safe crossing facilities, pedestrian priority design and continuous walking routes makes foot travel extremely inconvenient and high-risk.
The barren, monotonous street environment offers no visual attraction and discourages residents from choosing walking as a daily travel mode.
bikeability: No dedicated bicycle lanes or cycling exclusive space is provided on the roadway at all.
Mixed traffic with heavy trucks and private cars creates an extremely intimidating and high-risk environment for cyclists of all ages.
There is a complete lack of bicycle parking, route signage and other supporting facilities, making cycling an unfeasible and unsafe travel choice.
